title: Best VAT Software: 5 Tools to Calculate and File VAT
summary: Compare the best VAT software for calculating and filing VAT in the UK, EU and beyond, from end-to-end compliance platforms to MTD-ready accounting tools.
body_markdown:
The best VAT software for US companies is software that registers, calculates, validates, files and pays VAT in every country where you sell. That matters because US companies often owe[value added tax (VAT)](https://www.getsphere.com/blog/vat-gst-id) from their very first sale abroad. The UK has no VAT registration threshold for businesses based outside the country. EU VAT on digital sales to consumers is also due from the first sale.


So, VAT software has to do more than just calculate a rate. It has to register you with each tax authority, check customer VAT IDs, file each country's VAT returns and pay in local currency. This guide ranks five tools by the use case each one fits best, so you can build a shortlist that matches your business needs.


## 5 Best VAT Software at a Glance


[Sphere](https://www.getsphere.com/) is the best VAT software for end-to-end global VAT and US sales tax compliance in one platform. Fonoa is best for enterprise platforms that want to build VAT into their own stack through an API. Taxually is best for companies that want EU and UK VAT registration and filing handled as a service. Kintsugi fits US-first sellers that plan to add VAT later, and Xero fits a single UK entity filing Making Tax Digital (MTD) returns from its own books.

## What VAT Software Needs to Do for U.S. Companies


VAT software for US companies needs to cover the full VAT lifecycle. That means registration, VAT calculation, VAT ID checks, tax filing, payment and record keeping in each country. A tool that only calculates a rate leaves the hardest work to your finance team.


### Why U.S. Companies Owe VAT From the First Sale


US companies owe VAT from the first sale because most VAT countries give no threshold to foreign sellers. HMRC states that the UK registration threshold does not apply to non-established taxable persons. An overseas business must register if it makes any taxable supplies in the UK, no matter how small the business.


The EU works in a similar way for digital sales. A US business selling digital services to EU consumers owes VAT from the first sale. The €10,000 EU-wide threshold only applies to businesses based in the EU. However, instead of registering in all 27 EU countries, you can use the[EU One Stop Shop (OSS)](https://vat-one-stop-shop.ec.europa.eu/index_en) non-Union scheme. It lets you file one quarterly return for all your digital and other services sold to EU consumers. Goods shipped to EU consumers from outside the EU use a separate scheme, the Import One Stop Shop (IOSS).


The UK also controls how you file. Since April 1, 2022, every VAT-registered business must follow[Making Tax Digital for VAT](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/find-software-thats-compatible-with-making-tax-digital-for-vat) , regardless of taxable turnover. That includes overseas businesses registered for UK VAT unless HMRC grants an exemption. You must keep digital records and submit VAT returns through MTD-compatible software.


### Accurate Calculation and VAT ID Validation


Accurate VAT calculation depends on knowing whether your customer is a business. When you sell to a VAT-registered business in another country, the reverse charge usually applies. The customer accounts for the VAT, and you charge 0% on the invoice. Learn[more about the reverse charge here](https://www.getsphere.com/blog/reverse-charge-vat) .


The reverse charge should only apply when the customer's VAT ID passes a government database check. A format check only confirms that the number looks right. It does not confirm that the number is real or active. If you apply the reverse charge to a fake or expired VAT ID, the tax authority can bill you for the VAT you didn't collect.


In the EU, the official check is[the VAT Information Exchange System (VIES)](https://ec.europa.eu/taxation_customs/vies/) . Sphere validates VAT IDs against government databases in 36+ countries and runs format checks everywhere else. With Sphere, VAT ID lookups are free.


### Filing, Payment and Audit Trail


Good VAT software files a separate return for each country and pays each tax authority on time. Every country has its own form, due date and filing portal. In the UK, that means MTD e-filing straight to HMRC. In the EU, it may mean one OSS return plus local returns in countries where you have B2B sales.


Payment is just as important. Most tax authorities expect payment in local currency. International wires can add fees and delays, which raises the risk of late payment penalties.


Your software should also keep a full audit trail. You want records that run from registration to calculation to filing to payment. If an auditor asks questions, you can show every step.


### Input VAT Recovery and E-Invoicing


Input VAT recovery and e-invoicing are now part of the same VAT workflow as filing. Input VAT is the VAT you pay on business purchases, such as a conference booth in Germany or software bought from a UK vendor. In many countries, you can reclaim it. Learn[more about input tax here](https://www.getsphere.com/blog/input-tax) .


E-invoicing is also spreading fast. Countries like Italy,[Poland](https://www.getsphere.com/blog/e-invoicing-in-poland) ,[France](https://www.getsphere.com/blog/e-invoicing-in-france) , and[Belgium](https://www.getsphere.com/blog/e-invoicing-in-belgium) now require structured electronic invoices for many B2B sales. Others, like Germany, are phasing in mandates. See[current e-invoicing regulations in Europe here](https://www.getsphere.com/blog/e-invoicing-europe) .


It's important to note that most VAT software stops at the output VAT return. That means reclaiming VAT on purchases and issuing mandated e-invoices often fall to your team or an outside advisor.


## Compliance Platform vs Accounting Software for VAT


A compliance platform and accounting software solve different VAT problems. Accounting software files one entity's VAT return from its own books in one country. A compliance platform handles tax calculation at checkout or invoice, plus registration and filing across many countries.


Cloud accounting software like Xero, QuickBooks Online, Sage Business Cloud Accounting, FreeAgent, FreshBooks and Zoho Books is built for bookkeeping. These tools handle invoicing, bank reconciliation and often payroll software features. Many are MTD-compatible, so a UK business can submit VAT returns to HMRC directly. Some businesses that keep records in spreadsheets use bridging software to connect those records to HMRC.


That works well for a single UK company. But accounting software rarely calculates VAT for customers in other countries, registers you abroad or files an EU OSS return. It's also important to note that consumer tax software like TurboTax, H&R Block and TaxAct is built for US income tax returns. It doesn't handle VAT at all.


Here are the signs you've outgrown accounting-only VAT filing:


- **You owe VAT in a second country.** Each new country adds a new registration, return format and due date.
- **You sell digital services to EU consumers.** You now need EU OSS filing.
- **You make B2B sales at volume.** Each reverse-charge sale needs a validated VAT ID.
- **You also collect US sales tax.** Running VAT in one tool and US sales tax in another doubles your work.


## The 5 Best VAT Software Tools Ranked by Filing Need


The five best VAT software tools below are ranked by the filing need each one serves best. Each review covers standout capabilities, limitations, pricing and who the tool is best for.


### 1. Sphere: Best for End-to-End Global VAT and Sales Tax Compliance


[Sphere](https://www.getsphere.com/) is a global tax compliance platform that covers VAT, GST and US sales tax from registration through payment. It's built for US companies that sell physical goods, digital products or services across borders.


**Standout capabilities:**


- **Monitored tax rules:** Sphere's tax rules come from[TRAM](https://www.getsphere.com/blog/building-tram) , its AI research system, which reads and monitors tax law directly. A human expert approves each rule change. Then a fixed, deterministic engine does the actual tax calculation. Most competitors rely on manual research teams, but rule changes reach Sphere as they happen rather than after the fact when a researcher discovers them.
- **Broad coverage:** Sphere calculates VAT, GST and sales tax in 130+ jurisdictions, including US states and Canadian provinces. It also supports input VAT recovery in 32 jurisdictions and e-invoicing in 31.
- **In-house registration and filing:** Sphere's in-house team handles registrations, including EU OSS. Each country's return is reviewed and approved on its own, then Sphere submits it directly to the tax authority.
- **Local-currency payments:** Payments go to each tax authority in local currency. They're funded by ACH from your US bank account through an Airwallex account in your company's name. There are no international wires, and Sphere never holds your funds.
- **Integrations:** Sphere connects to NetSuite, Chargebee, Maxio, QuickBooks Online, Xero, Rillet and more.


**Limitations:** Sphere is a compliance platform, not accounting software. You'll still keep your general ledger in a tool like NetSuite or QuickBooks Online.


**Pricing:** Sphere charges a flat, all-inclusive $100 per region per month for the first 10 regions. There's no percentage of transaction value, no implementation fee and no charge for VAT ID lookups.


**Best for:** US companies that need US sales tax and international VAT handled in one platform.


### 2. Fonoa: Best for Enterprise Platforms Building VAT Into Their Own Stack


[Fonoa](https://www.getsphere.com/blog/fonoa-competitors) is an API-first indirect tax platform for large digital businesses. It covers tax ID validation, tax determination, e-invoicing, reporting and returns across a claimed 190+ jurisdictions.


**Standout capabilities:** Fonoa's modules plug into your own systems through a single API. That makes it a strong fit for marketplaces and platforms with in-house engineering teams and very high transaction volume.


**Limitations:** Fonoa is built for developers, not finance teams looking for a ready-made tool. You'll need engineering time to set it up. Registration and input VAT recovery are not part of its core published modules.


**Pricing:** Fonoa doesn't publish pricing. It quotes by module and transaction volume.


**Best for:** Enterprise platforms that want to build VAT logic directly into their own product.


### 3. Taxually: Best for EU and UK VAT Registration and Filing Services


Taxually is a VAT and sales tax compliance provider focused on registration and filing. It's well known among e-commerce and Amazon sellers in Europe. It also powers VAT filing for[Stripe](https://www.getsphere.com/blog/saas-tax-software) Tax users through a partner integration.


**Standout capabilities:** Taxually handles VAT registration in 100+ countries, monthly filings and fiscal representation where a country requires it. You upload or sync your sales data, and its team prepares and files the VAT returns.


**Limitations:** Taxually is more of a filing service than a full calculation engine. Fiscal representation in some countries can require a security deposit, and local fees can add to the bill.


**Pricing:** Taxually doesn't publish a rate card. It charges per registration and per filing, so costs grow with each new country.


**Best for:** E-commerce sellers that want EU and UK registration and filing handled for them.


### 4. Kintsugi: Best for US-First Sellers Planning to Add VAT Later


Kintsugi is a sales tax platform built mainly for US sales tax. It offers free nexus monitoring and automates US registrations, filings and remittance.


**Standout capabilities:** Kintsugi's pricing is simple for US sales tax. It integrates with QuickBooks, Stripe, Chargebee, Shopify and other tools.


**Limitations:** Kintsugi's EU and UK VAT coverage sits on its higher Premium plan, which is custom-priced. It doesn't offer input VAT recovery. Per-filing fees also add up quickly once you file monthly in many places.


**Pricing:** Kintsugi has a free monitoring plan. Its Starter plan begins at $75 per filing or registration. VAT coverage requires a custom quote.


**Best for:** US-first sellers that need sales tax now and expect to add VAT later.


### 5. Xero: Best for MTD Filing From a UK Entity’s Books


Xero is cloud accounting software that's popular with UK small businesses and their accountants. All paid Xero UK plans are HMRC-recognised for Making Tax Digital for VAT.


**Standout capabilities:** Xero keeps digital records, handles bank reconciliation and lets a VAT-registered business submit VAT returns directly to HMRC. Payroll is included from the Grow plan up.


**Limitations:** Xero files one entity's UK return from that entity's own books. It doesn't register you abroad, file EU OSS returns, validate VAT IDs against government databases or collect US sales tax.


**Pricing:** As of September 1, 2026, Xero UK plans range from £18 per month for Ignite to £70 per month for Ultimate, excluding VAT.


**Best for:** A single UK entity that wants MTD-compliant VAT returns from its accounting software.


## How to Choose the Best VAT Software for Your Filing Needs


The best VAT software for you depends on where you sell, who you sell to and how much of the VAT process you want handled for you. Use the questions below to compare your shortlist.


### Coverage, Registration and OSS


Start by checking which countries each tool files in itself. Some tools file directly with tax authorities. Others hand filing to partners or local advisors, which can add cost and slow things down.


Next, ask whether EU OSS registration and filing are included. Some companies pay their main tax software provider and then pay an advisory firm on top for OSS returns. Ask for a full list of what's included before you sign. For a deeper look at multi-country requirements, see our[guide to global VAT compliance](https://www.getsphere.com/blog/global-vat-compliance) .


### Rule Accuracy and VAT ID Validation


Ask who maintains the tax rules and how fast changes reach the engine. Many legacy providers, such as Avalara and Vertex, rely on manual research teams. Ask how a new rate or rule makes its way into your tax calculation, and how long that takes.


Then ask how the tool decides when to apply the reverse charge. The safest tools apply it only after a government[VAT ID](https://www.getsphere.com/blog/do-us-companies-have-a-vat-number) check, such as VIES in the EU or state-level checks in the US. A format check alone, which might allow an incorrect VAT ID or a fraudulent transaction to slip through, isn't enough to protect you in an audit.


### Filing Deadlines, Payments and Hidden Costs


Look closely at filing deadlines. Some providers require your data weeks before the actual due date. That shortens your month-end close and leaves little room to fix errors.


Next, check how payments reach each tax authority. International wire fees and currency conversion costs add up fast across many countries.


Finally, watch for pricing that grows with your sales. Per-transaction percentage fees can get expensive as revenue grows. Also watch out for VAT filing that's pushed to partner apps and billed separately. These seemingly small costs can amount to a large portion of your budget.


## Choose VAT Software That Files Everywhere You Sell


The right VAT software files everywhere you sell, not just where you started. US companies often owe VAT from their first sale abroad, so tax calculation alone isn't enough.


Accounting software like Xero or QuickBooks Online covers one entity's VAT return. Cross-border sellers need registration, filing, payment and input VAT recovery in one place. Sphere covers VAT and US sales tax end to end for a flat $100 per region per month.
